question: On identical recorded 25 Hz walking histories, how does direct multihorizon prediction compare with recursive one-step prediction and a frozen open checkpoint? Architecture selection on two previously assessed development people is exploratory.
source: UCI Daily and Sports Activities (Barshan and Altun), DOI 10.24432/C5C59F, CC BY 4.0, original archive SHA-256 f42ad7744ecf14151c9fa3a86dfb5b24de9d7cb7ffe956ef5de242983459c77e
window: The released right-arm sensor axes (zero-based columns 9,10,11); 16 past XYZ rows through cutoffs 15,31,47,63,79,95,111 within each 125-row clip. Only a09 and a10, segments 1..60. Each target is in that same file at origin+1,3,6,12 (40,120,240,480 ms nominal). Actual transport delay unavailable; units are stored sensor-native acceleration. No physiology, pose, force, cue or subject input.
direct: Use existing hash-verified training normalizer and 3-step residual ridge head. Fit only the three new ridge heads at h=1,6,12, using fixed alpha=.001 times n, centered design and unpenalized intercept on standardized displacement from the last observed XYZ. Each head uses all three axes. One dense output projects directly to four selected horizons.
recursive: Use exactly the new one-step head/normalizer and feed each predicted XYZ back into its own 16x3 input, advancing by one sample twelve times. No future observations, teacher forcing or retrospective correction. Direct and recursive must agree at h=1 to absolute tolerance 1e-11.
other_models: Repeat the last true observation. Compare zero-shot amazon/chronos-bolt-tiny revision a0e552de83495b5c28c14c71c374f3e33280b340, weights SHA-256 75068728d376d2bec670379eeef4bfb4d24c0cfe24d957451f8d19b447030a32, independently treating X,Y,Z as univariate 16-sample sequences. Request 12 steps, fixed default nine quantiles, float32 CPU, batch 32 XYZ histories, median vs measured. No tuning, adapters or fine-tuning. Different context feature sharing and previous data are part of the comparison, preventing isolation of backbone or pretraining effects. Unknown original pretraining corpus overlap. Existing dedicated 3-step Transformer and general Gaussian learner results remain h=3-only reference.
reconciliation: Hash and compare all 1680 previous reference row IDs and measured h=3 targets exactly before reusing stored ridge predictions; require recomputed h=3 agreement within 1e-11. Verify saved normalizer against input-only TRAIN moments to absolute tolerance 1e-12. All new fitted state is sealed before opening DEV.
scores: MAE per horizon, native units, at each person, activity, person/activity, pooled and axis. Per-horizon 95th absolute-error percentile for tail error, signed XYZ bias. Report horizon change in endpoint MAE without interpreting sensor error as spatial drift. For Chronos central 80 percent intervals, estimate marginal coverage, mean width and crossings per axis by horizon/person. No best-of-N, no probabilistic interpretation of direct point forecasts. Correlated windows in few people disallow independent-window population inference.
decision: A uniform direct win requires strictly smaller MAE than recursive, persistence and zero-shot Bolt in each of p5 and p6 at each of h=3,6,12. Report every failure and select descriptive choices by horizon when ranks switch. One-step is a required construction check. No reserve use or production promotion. A new open pretraining trial must retain source-specific splits and compare fixed forecast heads before any automatic weight adoption.
cost: Single CPU process, one BLAS thread, single inter-op, zero data workers, no GPU. Before any study member reads, choose 1 or 2 Torch intra-op threads from alternating matched CPU synthetic observations for the frozen Bolt batch; require float32 agreement within absolute 1e-4 on same test input. Report actual choice and startup, loading, fit and prediction time. Measure warm whole all-four-horizon model dispatch from a single complete 16x3 native-unit NumPy history through native output, median/p95 repeated timings, and batched DEV separately. Inference times exclude sensor acquisition/UI/transport. Also report separately h=3-only cost for existing Transformer and ridge. Torch/NumPy select CPU kernels; no direct GPU geometry available in this CPU build; Radeon training/inference remains unqualified. No wall-clock performance guarantee. Outputs scoped to an empty unique run directory.
